page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor providing 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 256 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware accelerators like GPUs are not included, but the instance features 2400 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth, achieving 218.61 GB/sec in large-block reads and 95.85 GB/sec in writes, both placing in the top quartile. Extended CPU instruction execution via AVX-512 and database operations in PassMark also register top-tier performance. In contrast, single-threaded throughput reflects older core architectures, resulting in lower-quartile scores in single-core stress testing and single-threaded compression algorithms. Multi-threaded general computation, Clang compilation, and Redis throughput remain within average performance brackets.

The combination of substantial high-speed local NVMe storage, significant network bandwidth, and high memory throughput makes the m5dn.16xlarge well configured for intermediate-tier caching clusters, clustered relational or NoSQL database nodes, high-throughput web serving, and ETL pipelines that process large datasets on scratch disks. The inclusion of dedicated instance storage avoids separate networked volume throughput overheads for temporary data operations.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.16xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based cloud instance powered by a 32-core, 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The platform features 256 GB of DDR4 memory, offering a balanced 1:4 resource ratio, paired with 2400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 75 Gbps baseline network throughput. In synthetic evaluations, the instance demonstrates upper-quartile memory bandwidth and database operation throughput, while single-threaded tasks fall into the lower quartile. The architecture contains no GPUs, prioritizing balanced multi-core density, high I/O throughput, and fast scratch disk storage. Consequently, the m5dn.16xlarge suits data-intensive services, relational and NoSQL databases, memory-backed distributed caches, and data transformation workloads requiring reliable local storage and wide network pipelines.
